newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Feb CPI not seen with nasty surprise - Bersani.
newsitem.headline: Italy Feb CPI not seen with nasty surprise - Bersani.

text.p: Italian industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said he did not expect any negative surprises from Italian inflation data this month and added the economic trend in early 1997 was better than the end of 1996.
Bersani, talking to reporters in Venice, said he expected inflation to continue its current trend. "We don't expect any negative surprises," he said.
Preliminary February consumer prices data are due to be released on Thursday and Friday.

Italian industrial production data last week showed a 3.1 percent fall year on year in December. Asked whether he could make a forecast on economic and production recovery after the data, Bersani said: "The start of this year will be probably a little better than the end of 1996."
He also did not rule out the possibilty of Italy making an additional minibudget, adding: "If it's to be done, it won't be of a very significant amount."
February CPI is expected on average to slow to 2.5 percent year on year from 2.6 percent in January, while the month on month rate is seen at 0.2 percent as in the previous month.
